routes.name: Unilateral Visa-Free Entry (trial policy)
routes.summary: Ordinary passport holders from 50 listed countries can enter for up to 30 days without a visa. It is a trial that runs through Dec 31, 2026 for most countries, so check before you book.

other: Ordinary passport only.
Allowed purposes: business, tourism, visiting family or friends, exchange, transit, sports events, conferences and exhibitions, study tours.
No work, study or news reporting.
Valid until Dec 31, 2026 for all except Russia (Dec 31, 2027) and Brunei (no end date).
Czech Republic is not on the list.
US, India, Mexico and others are not on this list. See the 240-hour transit record.

stay.note: Counted from the day after entry. Multiple entries allowed, no cap on total days right now. Longer stays need a visa in advance, or a stay permit from the local exit-entry office.

steps: Check your country is on the list.
Fly or travel in with an ordinary passport valid for your stay.
Carry proof of purpose like a hotel booking and onward ticket.

routes.name: 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit
routes.summary: Citizens of 57 countries can enter visa-free through any of 65 open ports in 24 provinces and regions and stay up to 10 days in permitted areas with an onward ticket to a third country or region. Work, study and news reporting are not allowed.

other: Ordinary passport only.
Must hold onward ticket with confirmed date and seat to a third country or region (not back to where you came from).
Stay limited to the designated area for that port.
Enter through any of 65 open ports in 24 provinces and regions.

routes.name: 24-Hour Direct Transit (no visa)
routes.summary: Nationals of any country can transit through China visa-free for up to 24 hours at any open port if they hold valid travel documents and an onward ticket with a confirmed seat. Stay in the restricted area of the port, or get a temporary entry permit first.

other: Needs valid travel documents and an onward international flight, ship or train ticket with a confirmed seat.
Leaving the port's restricted area needs a temporary entry permit from port immigration.

routes.name: Mutual Visa Exemption Agreements
routes.summary: China has mutual visa exemption agreements with 158 countries as of April 2025, but many cover only diplomatic or service passports. Some cover ordinary passports, with limits from 14 to 90 days.

other: Check the official list of agreements for your passport type and stay limit.

sources.label: NIA: List of mutual visa exemption agreements

routes.name: Hainan 30-Day Visa-Free Entry
routes.summary: Ordinary passport holders from 61 countries can enter Hainan without a visa and stay up to 30 days, within Hainan only. Allowed purposes include tourism, business, visits, medical care, conferences and sports.

other: Ordinary passport only.
Must enter through an open Hainan port.
No work or study.
Register with local police within 24 hours if not staying in a hotel.

routes.name: Regional Group Tour Visa-Free Entry
routes.summary: Tour groups can enter visa-free through set routes: Guangdong groups from Hong Kong or Macao (up to 6 days), ASEAN groups to Guilin or Xishuangbanna (6 days), and cruise groups via Shanghai (15 days).

other: Must be a group of two or more organized by a licensed travel agency.
Each route has its own ports and allowed areas.
Individuals from countries with a unilateral policy should use that instead.

sources.label: NIA: Regional Visa-Free Entry Policies

routes.name: Port Visa
routes.summary: A single-entry visa issued at a designated port for urgent reasons like emergencies or urgent business. Stay is up to 30 days.

other: Needs documents showing the competent Chinese authority approved the application.

sources.label: NIA: Port Visa and Regional Visa-Free Entry Policies

routes.name: L Visa (Tourist)
routes.summary: Tourist visa for people who want to visit China and are not covered by a visa-free policy. Apply online at consular.mfa.gov.cn/VISA/ and then at an embassy or visa center.

other: Needs travel documents like round-trip flight and hotel bookings, or an invitation letter from a person or company in China.
Consular officers decide validity, length of stay and number of entries case by case.

Fees are set by passport nationality and number of entries, not by visa category, and vary by embassy. US passport holders applying in the US pay USD 140 for a single entry (reduced rate valid until Dec 31, 2026). Check your local embassy.

routes.name: Z Visa (Work)
routes.summary: Visa for people who will work in China. Most applicants need the Notice for the Work Permit for Foreigners from the local human resources authority. After arrival you apply for a residence permit within 30 days.

other: One of these is required: Notice for the Work Permit for Foreigners; registration certificate of a foreign company representative office; approval for commercial performances plus Certificate of Short-term Work; or an offshore petroleum operations invitation letter from CNOOC.
Work of 90 days or less: apply before the start date on the notice.
Holders must apply for a residence permit within 30 days of entry, unless the visa says 30 days stay after entry.
Consular officers decide validity, length of stay and number of entries case by case.

Fees are set by passport nationality and number of entries, not by visa category, and vary by embassy. US passport holders applying in the US pay USD 140 for a single entry (reduced rate valid until Dec 31, 2026). Check your local embassy.

steps: Employer gets the Notice for the Work Permit for Foreigners.
Apply for the Z visa abroad.
Enter China and apply for a work residence permit within 30 days, unless your visa says 30 days stay after entry.

routes.name: Foreigner's Work Permit (Class A, B, C)
routes.summary: China sorts foreign workers into categories A (high-level talent), B (specialized talent) and C (other). Under the points route you need 85 or more points for A, and 60 to 84 for B.

other: Category A includes talent from national programs, scientists, young talent, and anyone scoring 85 points or more. A gets green-channel service.
Category B covers specialized talent, like a bachelor's degree plus 2 years of relevant work experience, plus language teachers and skilled workers.
Points are scored on salary (up to 20), work experience (up to 20), education (up to 20), Chinese language (up to 5), age and extras (up to 5).
Category C rules were not confirmed from an official page.
Rules are applied locally. Check your city's foreigner work permit office.

routes.name: Work Residence Permit
routes.summary: Residence permit you apply for within 30 days of entering China on a Z visa. It lets you live and work in China for the permit term.

other: Apply at the local exit-entry administration of the public security bureau within 30 days of entry, unless your Z visa says 30 days stay after entry.
Permit length and renewal rules were not confirmed from an official page.

routes.name: S1 and S2 Visas (Family of Foreigners in China)
routes.summary: S1 is for family of foreigners working or studying in China who need to stay over 180 days (spouse, parents, children under 18, parents-in-law). S2 is for family visits of 180 days or less, and wider family can use it.

Consular officers decide validity, length of stay and number of entries case by case.

routes.name: D Visa (Permanent Residence)
routes.summary: Visa for people approved for Chinese permanent residence. You need the Confirmation Form for Foreigner's Permanent Residence Status from the Ministry of Public Security. Apply for a residence permit within 30 days of arrival.

other: Needs the original and a copy of the Confirmation Form for Foreigner's Permanent Residence Status.
Residence permit application within 30 days of entry.

routes.name: Permanent Residence (Foreigner's Permanent Resident ID Card)
routes.summary: Known as the Chinese green card. The Ministry of Public Security approves it for foreigners who made a remarkable contribution to China or meet other set conditions. Years needed and thresholds were not confirmed.

other: Exit and Entry Administration Law, Art. 47: permanent residence goes to foreigners who made a remarkable contribution to China's economic and social development or meet other set conditions, approved by the Ministry of Public Security.
Holders can live and work in China and enter and leave with their passport and permanent residence permit.
Status can be canceled if you fail to reside in China for the prescribed time, among other reasons.
Years of residence and thresholds not confirmed from an official page.

sources.label: MFA Consular Services: Exit and Entry Administration Law

routes.name: Chinese Nationality by Naturalization
routes.summary: Foreigners and stateless people who respect China's Constitution and laws can be naturalized if they are near relatives of Chinese nationals, have settled in China, or have other legitimate reasons. The Ministry of Public Security approves it.

other: Must be willing to abide by China's Constitution and other laws.
The law sets no minimum years or language test. Approval is case by case.
Apply through the local public security bureau in China, or a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad.

sources.label: NIA: Nationality Law of the PRC

citizenship.note: China does not recognize dual nationality (Art. 3). A person naturalized as Chinese cannot keep foreign nationality (Art. 8).

routes.name: Chinese Nationality by Birth or Descent
routes.summary: A child born in China with at least one Chinese national parent is Chinese. Born abroad to a Chinese parent also counts, unless that parent has settled abroad and the child got foreign nationality at birth.

other: Born in China to stateless parents or parents of uncertain nationality who settled in China: also Chinese.
Born abroad: not Chinese if the Chinese parent(s) settled abroad and the child acquired foreign nationality at birth.

sources.label: NIA: Nationality Law of the PRC

citizenship.note: No dual nationality (Art. 3). Chinese nationals who settle abroad and take foreign nationality automatically lose Chinese nationality (Art. 9).

routes.name: Refugee Status and Asylum
routes.summary: China accepts asylum cases through its own process, but it is very rarely granted. Contact Chinese authorities directly.

other: Official category details could not be opened. Check the MFA visa portal at consular.mfa.gov.cn/VISA/ before relying on this.
